title: Adic criterion for flatness near the closed fibre
statement: Work over a scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme], with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] and universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal, and give $\operatorname{Spec}A$ a specified map to $S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $p:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Modules are on the small etale ringed site, with quasi-coherence and tensor pullback as in [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module, def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. A module is finitely presented if etale locally it is the cokernel of a map between finite rank free modules. Let $F$ be a finitely presented quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module. Write $Y_n=Y\times_A\operatorname{Spec}(A/I^n)$ and $F_n=F|_{Y_n}$ for tensor pullback [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Relative flatness means that on etale scheme charts the stalk of the module at a point is flat over the local ring at its image on the base [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Let $U\subseteq|Y|$ be the locus where $F$ is flat over $\operatorname{Spec}A$, using the point topology of [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Then $U$ is open. If every $F_n$ is flat over $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I^n)$ for $n\geq1$, then $p^{-1}(V(I))\subseteq U$, where $V(I)$ is the set of prime ideals containing $I$. Completeness of $A$, separatedness of $p$, and properness of the support are not required; the conclusion only asserts flatness along this closed inverse image.

source.place: Tag 08VP, lemma-flatness-over-Noetherian-ring, statement and openness assertion in its proof; finitely presented quasi-coherent modules are coherent here by spaces-cohomology.tex, lemma-coherent-Noetherian.

proof.text: Fix any affine etale chart $e:W=\operatorname{Spec}B\to Y$. By [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus], the restriction of $F$ corresponds to $\widetilde M$, where $M=F(W)$ is a finitely presented $B$-module. In particular $M$ is generated by the images of a finite basis in a finite presentation. The composite $W\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is locally of finite presentation by the chart definition [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] gives a finite presentation of $B$ as an $A$-algebra. This is a finite-type presentation after forgetting the finiteness of the relations, so $B$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. This argument applies independently on each affine chart and requires no quasi-compactness of $Y$.

source.place: Tag 08VP (lemma-flatness-over-Noetherian-ring), affine-chart reduction; Algebra Tag 00FN and Morphisms Tag 01TQ supply the finiteness hypotheses of Algebra Tag 0523.

proof.text: For $w\in W$ corresponding to $\mathfrak q\subset B$, put $\mathfrak p=A\cap\mathfrak q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization] the ordinary stalk of the chart module is $M_{\mathfrak q}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization], flatness of this module over $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is equivalent to flatness over $A$. The pointwise chart-independence lemma [lem-sfb-space-module-flat-point-chart-independence] therefore identifies $e^{-1}(U)$ with $\{\mathfrak q:M_{\mathfrak q}\text{ is flat over }A\}$. This is open by [lem-weil-pbc-openness-of-flatness], using the finite presentations from step 1. On every etale scheme chart the affine subopens cover by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], and they are again chart objects by [def-trf-space-module-scheme-restriction]; so the inverse image of $U$ is open on that entire chart. The final-topology definition [def-a1-space-point-topology] now says precisely that $U$ is open in $|Y|$.

source.place: Tag 08VP (lemma-flatness-over-Noetherian-ring), first sentence (openness), expanding the affine proof of theorem-openness-flatness via Algebra Tag 00RC and the chart topology.

proof.text: Assume all $F_n$ are flat over $A/I^n$. For the chart of step 1 form $W_n=W\times_A\operatorname{Spec}(A/I^n)$. It is an etale scheme chart of $Y_n$ by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The affine fibre-product formula [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies its ring with $B\otimes_A A/I^n=B/I^nB$: the maps are $b\otimes\bar a\mapsto\overline{ba}$ and $\bar b\mapsto b\otimes1$. By the normalized composition of tensor pullbacks [def-sfb-space-module-tensor-composition], restriction of $F_n$ to $W_n$ is the pullback of the chart module on $W$. Under the scheme Zariski-etale pullback comparison [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] and the affine pullback formula [lem-weil-pbc-tilde-pullback-base-change], its ordinary module is $(B/I^nB)\otimes_B M=M/I^nM$. Explicitly $\bar b\otimes m\mapsto bm\bmod I^nM$, with inverse $m\bmod I^nM\mapsto1\otimes m$; the balanced relations and annihilation by $I^n$ verify both maps. The flatness hypothesis on $F_n$, tested on this chart, and the affine characterization in [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over] imply that $M/I^nM$ is flat over $A/I^n$ for every $n\geq1$.

source.place: Tag 08VP (lemma-flatness-over-Noetherian-ring), affine reduction before application of Algebra Tag 0523; omitted tensor-pullback and quotient identifications written explicitly (Schemes Tags 01I4, 01I9).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-powers] to the ring map $A\to B$, ideal $I$, and module $M$. Both rings are Noetherian and $M$ is finite by step 1; all its quotient flatness hypotheses are step 3. Consequently $M_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $A$ whenever $\mathfrak q\supseteq IB$. By the identification of step 2, all these chart points belong to $e^{-1}(U)$. A point $w\in W$ maps into $V(I)$ exactly when $I\subseteq A\cap\mathfrak q$, equivalently $IB\subseteq\mathfrak q$. Every point of $Y$ lifts to a scheme atlas by [def-trf-algebraic-space], and then to an affine open by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]; it remains an etale chart by [def-trf-space-module-scheme-restriction]. Hence every point of $p^{-1}(V(I))$ belongs to $U$. No completion or support argument has entered the proof.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q07-871940f0d (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item. Its statement is unchanged from live/base, the live item is still unsplit (no group has superseded it) and there is no re-split note. Source: 08VP (spaces-more-morphisms.tex:6089). Its typos, X for X_n and 'flat over X' for flat over S, are correctly reported, and the item already carried the corrected reading. I checked 0523 (algebra.tex:23808) and 00RC (algebra.tex:33407) against their nodes hypothesis by hypothesis. Step 1 gets a finitely presented M from the qcoh chart calculus, A->B of finite presentation by the chart test with b=id and 01TQ, and B Noetherian by 00FN. Step 2 identifies the stalk with M_q, moves flatness between A_p and A, uses the new pointwise node to get e^{-1}(U)={q: M_q flat over A}, gets openness from 00RC, and finishes with the affine basis and the final topology. Step 3 identifies the ring of W_n with B/I^nB and the restricted module with M/I^nM via gamma, the Zariski-etale comparison and the tilde base change. One minor point: the fibre-product citation for W_n being etale over Y_n is loose, because its covering clause needs a jointly surjective family, but the fact is immediate from def-trf-algebraic-space. Step 4 applies 0523 with all four hypotheses verified; IB in q iff I in A cap q; atlas plus affine basis covers p^{-1}(V(I)). The new node lem-sfb-space-module-flat-point-chart-independence is a correct statement-only 05VU node: the 05VU proof works for an arbitrary diagram with V=T and b=id, so 'some chart' and 'every chart' are both equivalent to the geometric-stalk condition. Edge cases checked: empty X, chart points missing over x, the zero module. It is not a duplicate. The existing lem-sfb-space-module-flat-chart-test is the global atlas-wide form and does not give the pointwise locus step 2 needs; the node is a strengthening of it (merge advisory only). 04NG strict-local-flatness and 05X3 flat-locus base change are about morphisms, and lem-pc-relative-flat-module-stalk is for schemes only. It does not restate a clause of the item. Accepted tool_uses: 00RC, 0523, the tilde pullback, trf fibre products, the trf Zariski-etale equivalence, all generic. Batch-5: every listed trf citation is a general definition (algebraic space, qcoh module, etale module functors, scheme restriction, point topology) or a generic qcoh/chart tool (qcoh affine-chart calculus, gamma tensor composition, Zariski-etale equivalence). None is a step of the proof of the trace formula or of Poincare duality, so all are accepted. No SGA citation. No changes.
